outcome: Prevalence of interventions/complications based on the Maternity Safety Thermometer (MST)
Association between MST scores and sociodemographic, clinical, and obstetric factors
cohort: 260 postpartum women admitted to the maternity ward of a tertiary hospital between October 10th and December 30th, 2020.
finding: One-third of the participating women had two or more complications/interventions (high temperature by the MST), and factors associated with this high temperature were being of social class A or B, having a previous cesarean section, and being hospitalized during pregnancy.
mod_finding: 38.5% of participants had abdominal scarring (cesarean section)
26.5% had perineal scarring (2nd-degree tear or greater - spontaneous or by episiotomy).
